description: Returns the current state of one video generation: a SINGLE, IMMEDIATE read that waits for nothing. WHEN: only when you need one job's raw fields now (what it cost, whether it was refunded, why it failed). It is not how you wait (`wait_for_generation` is) and not how you show a video (the create already opened the card; `show_generation` brings back an earlier one). Do not poll it. When the user says something failed or looks wrong, read the job and report its actual state and charges instead of arguing from memory. `status` is `queued`, `processing`, `succeeded` (`url` is the finished file) or `failed` (terminal: `error.message` says why). STORY EPISODES also carry `story.stage`: `frames_review` means the run WAITS FOR THE USER (show the frames, do not poll); `writing_failed` is TERMINAL with `status: "failed"` (nothing charged, cast saved: offer a fresh `generate_story_video` with the same `cast_member_ids`); at `ready_to_render` the episode `url` is only the raw stitched preview. After a render, `story.render` is the LATEST render's verdict: `stage: "rendered"` with `story.render.status: "succeeded"` makes `story.render.url` the FINAL file; `failed` means that render was refunded and the episode can render again. OUTPUT: tell the user the media URL and one line about it, not raw JSON or job ids.

id.description: The job id returned by `generate_video` or `generate_story_video` (the documented way to read a story episode's stage); `list_videos` carries it too.

name: get_video
title: Get an AI video job
